key_insight: FutureSim replays real-world events in chronological order so agents can be evaluated on their ability to forecast and adapt to information that arrives after their training cutoff, providing a realistic temporal benchmark for adaptation.
problem_solved: Current evaluations lack grounded, time-ordered scenarios that test an agent's ability to update beliefs and make forecasts as real events unfold; FutureSim fills this gap by providing chronological replays of news/events and resolved outcomes for realistic adaptive evaluation.
method: Construct grounded simulations by chronologically replaying real news/articles and event streams, exposing agents to information as it historically arrived.
Require agents to forecast future events and act/interact while new evidence arrives, then compare predictions to resolved outcomes that occur later in the replay.
Measure adaptation with metrics like forecasting accuracy, calibration, update latency, and downstream task performance to quantify how well agents incorporate new information.
impact: This enables practitioners to measure and improve agents' real-world adaptability and forecasting under time-evolving conditions, guiding development of safer, more robust systems for deployment in dynamic environments.
visual_elements: Timeline replay diagram: chronological news/articles with agent predictions overlaid and later ground-truth resolution markers.
Agent loop schematic: observe (incoming news) -> predict (forecast) -> act -> update beliefs/state.
Metric dashboard: time-series charts for forecasting accuracy, calibration, and update latency across the replay.
Example news card pair: original article at time t, agent's forecast, and later resolved outcome for quick qualitative inspection.
paper_title: FutureSim: Replaying World Events to Evaluate Adaptive Agents
paper_authors: Shashwat Goel, Nikhil Chandak, Arvindh Arun, Ameya Prabhu, Steffen Staab
